steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here’s a quick rundown of the key differences:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA: deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen)  
   • RNA: ribose  

2. Strandedness  
   • DNA: almost always double-stranded helix  
   • RNA: usually single-stranded (but can fold into complex shapes)  

3. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA: A, T (thymine), G, C  
   • RNA: A, U (uracil) replaces T, G, C  

4. Function & location  
   • DNA: stable, long-term storage of genetic blueprint (mostly in the nucleus)  
   • RNA: transient carriers and processors of genetic information (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA, etc.), travels to ribosomes for protein synthesis.
